properties.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor real parcel boundary, blklot 8711020 (671-691 China Basin St); name/address from press coverage
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-19 after the owner flagged missing coverage in this area on review: Sister Lillian Murphy Community, a 152-unit affordable housing development (studios to 5-bedroom units, serving multigenerational households) at 671-691 China Basin St, developer Mercy Housing, celebrated in a City/Mayor London Breed event in April 2022. All 11 DataSF building-footprint pieces that fall within this address's own Assessor lot (blklot 8711020) were unioned into one multipolygon -- a courtyard-style building typically LIDAR-detects as several disconnected roof sections, the same pattern already seen for The Beacon. CORRECTED 2026-09-19: this record's own site field read 'Mission Bay North' since it was added -- wrong; a point-in-polygon check against DataSF's official redevelopment-area boundary (data/raw/redevelopment_project_areas.geojson) places it in 'Mission Bay - South', and it corresponds to the OCII plan's Block 6 West (671-691 China Basin St fronts China Basin St, Block 6's own north boundary per the plan drawing, immediately west of the already-confirmed Block 6 East). Neighboring records added in the same original pass (MB360, MB360 1200 4th St) were correctly tagged Mission Bay South, so this was an isolated mistake, not a systemic one. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-19: the owner flagged this record's shape as visibly funky on the rendered map. The 11-piece footprint union only ever covered the building's separate roof/wing sections (892 sqm total), leaving the courtyard, connecting sections and most of the complex unshaded even though they're part of the same real building. Replaced with blklot 8711020's own real Assessor parcel boundary (7363 sqm, a single clean polygon) -- visually confirmed against satellite to cover the whole real building complex (both wings and the courtyard) while correctly excluding the neighboring building across the internal walkway to its east; checked for overlap against the already-tracked 6E parcel (blklot 8711505) and found none. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: corrections to two areas above: the blklot 8711020 parcel is 7,363 sq m only in Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), which inflates area about 1.6x at this latitude; its true area is about 4,590 sq m. Likewise the 11-piece footprint union is about 556 sq m, not 892 sq m (also a Web Mercator figure). It is still a single polygon with no overlap with the 6E parcel (blklot 8711505); the two parcels touch. The shape shown on the map is unchanged. 2026-10-12 audit corrections (text only; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type): (1) 'celebrated in a City/Mayor London Breed event in April 2022' rests on SF YIMBY, whose article is dated April 5, 2022 (a publication date): 'The city of San Francisco and its beloved Mayor London Breed is celebrating the inauguration of a new housing develoment at 691 China Basin Street'. The article does not give the date of the event, so April 2022 is the article's date, not an event date. (2) 'corresponds to the OCII plan's Block 6 West' is Pier & Point's own reading of the plan drawing by position (no source read names the block for this address); it is not stated by a source.
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- DataSF Assessor real parcel boundary (blklot 8711020), name/address from press coverage; not a hand trace or plan estimate. The date of the City and Mayor event is not stated by the source read (SF YIMBY, published April 5, 2022), and no opening date has been confirmed.
properties.notes: No opening date is confirmed: the only dated source read is SF YIMBY's article published April 5, 2022, which reports the City and Mayor celebrating the new housing but does not give the date of the event; unit-mix figures (studio-5BR) not verified against a primary developer source.
